newsitem.title: USA: NYSE mulls growth at long-time downtown site.
newsitem.headline: NYSE mulls growth at long-time downtown site.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Monday it was considering an expansion of its 1903 landmark lower Manhattan site under a plan that includes a glass atrium across Broad Street to the old J.P. Morgan building.
The exchange recently has been looking to expand its current 18 Broad St. site at the corner of Broad and Wall Streets, or relocate, to accomodate a sharp rise in trading volume.
The NYSE average daily volume is 430 million shares, up from 346 million last year and 141 million ten years ago.

"This is a plan that we are bringing to the city to talk about the feasibilty of implementing," an NYSE spokesman said, noting the design would require New York City approval because of the proposed closure of a section of a street.
He said the construction -- to add 20,000 square feet of new trading floor -- has not yet been voted on by the NYSE board. The NYSE currently has 36,000 square feet of trading floor.
The first stop in the city approval process, the spokesman said, is the office of Mayor Rudolph Guiliani. The mayor's office did not immediately comment on the proposal.

A source at the exchange said the project -- expected to cost at least $100 million and take three to five years to complete -- would be funded from cash held by the NYSE, which amounted to $480 million at the end of 1995.
"The plans are to encase in a glass atrium the area between the existing face of the exchange across the street to the old J.P. Morgan building," the NYSE spokesman said.
A J.P. Morgan official said the firm still houses some operations at the Broad Street building, though the headquarters have moved several blocks away to 60 Wall St.

"We are happy to work with the exchange in any way that we can to support their remaining in New York," a J.P. Morgan spokesman said, adding that the exchange informed the firm as a courtesy and the plan does not include any destruction of the Morgan building.
